voiceover:
[conversational] Stop paying a photographer for every single product shot.

Stay till the end, because skipping 3 checks can get your listing suppressed.

One phone photo can become a studio shot, mannequin display and sale poster.

Open ChatGPT, tap plus, Add photos & files, and pick your photo. Then paste a saved prompt from your Notes app. [playful] Call them /studio, /mannequin and /flashsale. They're just your labels, not real commands.

Include this line: [confident] "Keep the product exactly as in my photo. Change only background, lighting and styling."

[serious] Honest catch: AI can change your logo or colour, so proofread poster text.

Here are the 3 checks. One, match the real item: colour, shape, logo. Two, keep one real, unedited photo, because Etsy requires it. Three, disclose AI edits on Etsy, and tag Amazon if a realistic AI person appears. Rules vary by marketplace and region, so check yours.

Which marketplace do you sell on?

Send this to the friend who books a photographer for every product.

Hack saved?

title: STOP PAYING PHOTOGRAPHERS

✅ Run the 3 checks: match the real item, keep one real photo, disclose AI edits

topic: Turn a plain phone photo of your product into studio-quality e-commerce images, a mannequin display and a flash-sale poster using short saved ChatGPT prompts, with a checklist for keeping the product accurate

pick.topic: Turn a plain phone photo of your product into studio-quality e-commerce images, a mannequin display and a flash-sale poster using short saved ChatGPT prompts, with a checklist for keeping the product accurate
pick.angle: Stop paying a photographer for every product shot, but check these 3 things before you upload AI photos to your store, because marketplaces and customers punish images that misrepresent the product
pick.why: 2.16M views and 37,967 comments, by far the highest comment count in the list. It is a direct small-business use case (product photos and sale posters) and is easy to show in 3 steps. The 'codes' format was only covered as a study set, so product photography is a new topic for us.

research.tool: ChatGPT Images (ChatGPT image generation and editing, current model: ChatGPT Images 2.6)
research.availability: <cite index="1-4">Create new images and edit existing ones in ChatGPT.</cite> <cite index="6-4">OpenAI's Images help page says ChatGPT Images is on all tiers.</cite> <cite index="14-15">Free has limited image creation, Go more, Plus more complex image creation, Pro unlimited subject to abuse guardrails.</cite> It runs on web, iOS and Android. OpenAI publishes no fixed daily image count.
steps: Open ChatGPT (web, iOS or Android app) and start a new chat.

Add your phone photo: <cite index="9-6">select +, then Add photos & files, or drag the image into the message box or paste it.</cite> On phone, <cite index="2-3">you first need to grant ChatGPT access to your camera roll.</cite>

Paste your saved prompt, for example a studio e-commerce prompt, a mannequin display prompt or a flash-sale poster prompt. Keep the prompts in a Notes app, a ChatGPT Project or Custom Instructions. Include one line like 'Keep the product exactly as in my photo: same shape, colour, logo, text and proportions. Change only background, lighting and styling.' Send.

Review the result against your original photo. To fix one thing, <cite index="9-1">describe the change in the chat or highlight an area with Select.</cite> Give one change at a time and say what must stay unchanged.
Find or download the finished image: <cite index="1-15">all images you create are automatically saved under Images.</cite> You can also open More, then Images, to start from there.
Before uploading to a store, run the 3-point accuracy check in the notes. Your real photo must still match the AI image.
facts: <cite index="1-10">To edit an image, select an image generated by ChatGPT Images or upload an existing image, then describe the change you want.</cite>

<cite index="1-5">OpenAI says ChatGPT Images 2.6 generates images faster and keeps details more consistent from one edit to the next.</cite> Wikipedia gives its release date as <cite index="12-6">November 4, 2026.</cite>
US plan prices (third-party roundups, not checked on chatgpt.com/pricing): <cite index="44-1">Free at $0, Go at $8, Plus at $20, and three Pro tiers at $100, $200 and $500.</cite>

<cite index="15-4">OpenAI does not publish how many images ChatGPT can generate for free.</cite> Third parties report about 2-3 per rolling 24 hours, and individual reports range from 1 to 8. Say 'a few a day on Free, limits vary'.
Third-party reports put Plus at about 40-50 images per 3-hour window. OpenAI has not published this number, so avoid stating it as fact.
<cite index="9-18">On Free, each photo counts toward a limit of 3 file uploads per day.</cite> This comes from a third-party guide, so treat it as approximate.

Slash commands are not built into ChatGPT. <cite index="34-8">Slash shortcuts for image prompts are not official universal ChatGPT slash commands.</cite> <cite index="34-4">They are reusable shorthand your team defines, saves and expands into a full prompt.</cite>
Custom Instructions limits: <cite index="32-1,32-2">Free and Go users can save up to 1,500 characters; Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Education users up to 5,000.</cite>

Amazon: <cite index="29-4,29-5">The product image guide does not ban images made or edited with AI. It requires every image to accurately represent the product and match the title. The main image must be realistic and professional-quality, showing the product's real scale, quantity and colour.</cite>
Amazon main image spec: <cite index="26-14">pure white RGB 255,255,255 background, product at 85% of the frame, no text or props, accurate scale and colour.</cite>

Amazon AI-people tag: <cite index="29-6">if an image or video contains photorealistic people entirely generated by AI, you must tag the file before uploading it.</cite> This matters for a mannequin or model display if ChatGPT adds a realistic person. A plain mannequin is not a person.

Etsy (update dated October 22, 2026): <cite index="50-2,50-3">The listing must include at least one unedited photo of the actual item against a real background, and all photos must accurately represent the item a buyer will receive.</cite>
Etsy also says: <cite index="50-5">If you use AI to edit any of your listing photos, note whether images were edited in your listing description.</cite>

Etsy refund risk: if a listing breaks the image rules and a buyer opens a case because the item is materially different, <cite index="56-8">you may be responsible for refunding the buyer.</cite> Etsy's 'Report this item' options now include 'It uses misleading AI-generated images'.
do_not_claim: Do not say /mannequindisplay, /flashsale or /productphotography are real ChatGPT commands. Typing them does nothing on its own. They only work as your own labels for prompts you have saved, or if ChatGPT is told what they mean.
Do not say 'in 1 second'. Generation takes time, and Free accounts have image limits.
Do not say 'studio quality every time' or 'ready to upload'. AI edits can change shape, colour, logo, text, stitching or proportions, so every output needs checking against the real product.
Do not say the '50+ ready-made prompts' exist as a verified product. It is the other creator's lead magnet, collected through a DM giveaway. Say 'save your own 3 prompts'.
Do not claim unlimited free images or a specific free daily number as official.
Do not say Amazon or Etsy ban AI images. Amazon has no blanket ban. Etsy allows AI-edited secondary photos but now requires an unedited real photo plus accurate representation.

Do not say a fully AI-generated product is fine for the Amazon main image. It must show the real product accurately on pure white, so use AI mainly for secondary or lifestyle images, or edit a real photo.

Do not say the poster text will be perfect. Check every price, percentage and date on a flash-sale poster by hand. Text rendering errors are the usual risk, and Amazon main images cannot carry text anyway.
criticism: Accuracy drift: <cite index="9-14">the edit comes back as a new image, so check faces, text and edges before you use it.</cite>
Marketplace risk: <cite index="24-12">listings get suppressed when an image misrepresents the product, with a wrong colour, invented features or distorted size.</cite>
Etsy forbids <cite index="52-10">using AI to alter photos so an item looks better, higher quality or materially different than what the buyer will receive.</cite>
Limits: image generation is capped on Free and OpenAI publishes no number, so batch work for a whole catalogue may need a paid plan.
<cite index="49-6">Free and Go carry ads; Plus and above do not.</cite> This is minor, but the creator's 'free' framing is incomplete.

ui.platforms: web (chatgpt.com), iOS, Android. The steps are the same on each, with small layout differences.
screens: Screen 1, ChatGPT home: left sidebar on web with a new chat option, an 'Images' entry, and chat history. In the centre is the message box (composer) with a '+' button at the bottom-left of the box. Following the sidebar order: 'Images' sits in the sidebar, and the same page can be reached via More > Images. Default theme follows the device setting (light or dark), so it is unverified which one appears.

Screen 2, tap '+' in the composer. The menu shows 'Add photos & files', plus camera and other options. Pick the product photo from Photos or Files. A thumbnail of the photo appears above the text box.
Screen 3, type or paste the saved prompt next to the thumbnail and press the send arrow (up-arrow button at the right of the composer).

Screen 4, ChatGPT replies in the chat with the generated image. Tapping the image opens it full-screen, where there is a 'Select' tool to highlight an area, and download or share options. On mobile, tap the image to open full-screen.
Screen 5, 'Images' page: all generated images are saved here, with a 'Create Image' button to start a new one. Templates for posters and similar designs are on this page.

Screen 6, comparison view for the checklist: put the original phone photo and the AI image side by side and check colour, logo and text, shape and proportions, and details such as seams, buttons and ports. You can build this as a simple split screen.

research.visuals: Show the real phone photo next to the AI-generated studio shot, mannequin display and flash-sale poster. Then show a split-screen comparison with 3 checkmarks. The generated images can be real outputs, or the ChatGPT screens can be recreated. Only a real screen recording can show the exact live UI and the output quality, because results vary by product. Use your own product photos and do not imply a result is guaranteed.
research.notes: The trick works (upload a photo, then prompt an edit), but the popular reel misleads about slash commands. Frame it as 'save your own 3 prompts' under names like /studio, /mannequin and /flashsale. THE 3 CHECKS, based on verified policy: (1) Product accuracy: colour, shape, size, logo, text, included parts and flaws must match the real item, and the Etsy rule against making the item look better applies. (2) Keep a real unedited photo of the actual item on a real background. Etsy now requires at least one (Oct 22, 2026 update, some exceptions by category). For Amazon, keep the main image compliant (pure white, 85% fill, no text or props), and use AI mainly for secondary images. (3) Disclose and tag: note AI edits in the Etsy listing description, and add Amazon's contains-synthetic-performer tag if a photorealistic AI person appears. Also proofread all poster text and prices. Policies change often, so say 'as of Nov 2026, check your marketplace's current rules'. Some figures (image caps, exact prices on chatgpt.com/pricing, exact UI labels and default theme) come from third-party sources or were not verified live. Confirm on the live pages before recording. The chatgpt.com/pricing 'Plus' text is unverified on the live page. I did not find the Amazon Seller Central primary page in search, so the Amazon points rely on secondary summaries of Amazon's Product image guide. Shopify, Meesho, Flipkart and Google Merchant Center rules were not checked, so do not state them. The reel's audience is Tamil-speaking, so mention that rules vary by marketplace and region.
